scope: Application-owned sender congestion detector: the bwe.BWE implementation LiveKit selects when rtc.congestion_control.use_send_side_bwe is true. Covers the send_side_bwe facade, congestionDetector, packetTracker, packetGroup, probePacketGroup, trafficStats weighted loss, the twcc measure, trend detector, probe regulator and the ccutils goal/result/info/signal values, plus the pinned-Go stimulus campaign (operations.tsv -> golden.tsv) and the Rust side of that differential. NOT covered: the pacer/prober that actually emits probe packets, the stream allocator that consumes the reported capacity, receiver-side REMB (remote_bwe), the str0m transport that owns the stamped transport-wide sequence numbers, and any launched-MAIN or official-SDK acceptance.
supported_domain: Time values are declared-microsecond integers read by the pinned Go as time.Duration, as int64 nanoseconds of the monotonic clock, or as a float count of seconds, and each read is keyed by a name that says which. i64 clock differences wrap with Go int64 semantics instead of trapping. TWCC reference-time and sequence arithmetic stay inside their 16-bit quanta, including the wrap. Out-of-range or architecture-dependent Go float-to-integer conversions are recorded as unsupported rather than asserted equivalent.

stimulus_units.policy: Every time value in operations.tsv is a count of MICROSECONDS and every time-valued leaf key declares that in its name (`*_us`). The Go generator refuses a bare, `_ns`, `_ms` or `_s` spelling on a time key, and the Rust reader `oracle_input.rs::time_us` refuses the same set, so a value can only cross the boundary at a declared scale.
stimulus_units.why: Upstream disagrees about units inside one struct family, so position alone is ambiguous: `ProbeClusterGoal.Duration` is a `time.Duration`, the prober's `ProbeClusterResult.StartTime/EndTime` are int64 nanoseconds stamped by `mono.UnixNano()` in `pacer/probe_observer.go`, and `congestionDetector.rtt` is a float count of seconds. The pre-units campaign passed `end=600000000` where the Rust stimulus helper read the same digits as milliseconds, which modelled a 600 s cluster instead of Go's 600 ms while the row text looked correct.
stimulus_units.separate: Counts that are not durations keep their own declared meaning: `ref=` is a number of 64 ms TWCC reference-time quanta and the packet timestamps in `tracker.rs` are RTP microseconds.

adaptations: One serialized input stream replaces upstream's per-connection goroutine ownership, because the Rust transport has a single owner of Rtc

str0m assigns the transport-wide extension value, so this port reconstructs the extended sequence counter from the stamped value instead of handing one out (`RecordPacketSendAndGetSequenceNumber`), and meters `packet_bytes` = header + payload + padding as `pacer/base.go:113` does, not the payload-only size the Pion interceptor uses

Probe observer stamps are nanoseconds since the owner's own `Instant` origin rather than `mono.UnixNano()`; only differences of those stamps are ever read, so the epoch choice is unobservable and the clock stays monotonic

The oracle clock origin is `time.Unix(1000, 0)` and the Rust rows are offsets from the same row zero, which is what makes an unset base stamp printable as `-1000000000` on the Go side and `NO_BASE_US` on the Rust side

Returned state changes replace the locked asynchronous BWEListener notification; embedding `bwe.NullBWE` upstream means `HandleREMB`, `GetChannelCapacity` and the bandwidth-observer calls are no-ops in this mode, so the REMB driver branch is not faked here
`SendSideFeedback::Discontinuity` has no upstream counterpart: it is the Rust boundary's honest reaction to a retired send history the estimator depends on, and the driver recreates the owner

Actual source Go golden keeps the original policy bodies and only unifies package namespaces, stubs the logger/zapcore boundary, supplies the deterministic clock and pins the packet tracker's random transport-wide sequence start to 1<<15; no Rust output generates an expected value
